name: Z-Axis Nuclear Depth Measurement
description:
You are a cell biologist investigating nuclear morphology. The standard XY view of a microscope only shows the 'top-down' shape of a cell, but you need to determine how flat or deep the nucleus is (Z-axis thickness).

Your task:
1. Open the HeLa cell Z-stack from `~/ImageJ_Data/raw/HeLa_stack/` (this is a folder of images or a TIFF stack).
2. Select the 'Straight Line' tool and draw a line across the center of a clearly visible nucleus.
3. Perform a 'Reslice' operation (Image > Stacks > Reslice) to generate a side-view (cross-section) of that nucleus. Use default settings (Top, 1.0 micron spacing).
4. In the new Reslice window, use the Straight Line tool to measure the vertical height (depth) of the nucleus from top to bottom.
5. Measure this distance (Analyze > Measure).
6. Save the measurement result to `~/ImageJ_Data/results/nucleus_depth.csv`.
7. Save the resliced image itself to `~/ImageJ_Data/results/nucleus_reslice.tif`.

Note: The measurement in the CSV must represent the Z-depth (vertical axis in the reslice), not the XY diameter.
